home.noAdminBody: Some system folders stay hidden, and the system cleaner is not available.

admin.unixHint: To get root rights, close Lustro and start it as root (for example with sudo).

settings.protectedHint: The root folder, the system folders (/usr, /etc, /var, /opt and others), home folders and their standard folders, and SSH and GPG keys. Lustro never deletes them.
settings.allowAppFoldersHint: Only as root. You can then delete app folders inside /opt, with a warning each time.
settings.lowSpaceHint: Sends a notification when a drive has less free space than this. Once a day per drive.
settings.startWithWindowsHint: Starts in the tray, without root rights.

scan.deniedNote_one: Lustro could not read 1 folder. Run it as root to include it.
scan.deniedNote_other: Lustro could not read {{count}} folders. Run it as root to include them.

explore.appFolder: App folder in /opt. You can delete it, but you must confirm a warning.
explore.appFolderLocked: App folder in /opt. To delete it, run Lustro as root and turn on Settings > Allow deleting app folders.
explore.denied: Only root can read this folder.

files.binNote: Files in the Trash still use space. Empty the Trash, or use Shift+Delete to delete permanently.

del.recycleNote: You can restore it from History or from the Trash.
del.permanentWarn: You cannot undo this. The item does not go to the Trash.
del.appWarn_one: This item is inside /opt. The app can stop working, and the package manager can still list it as installed. If you can, remove it with the package manager instead.
del.appWarn_other: {{count}} items are inside /opt. These apps can stop working, and the package manager can still list them as installed. If you can, remove them with the package manager instead.

dupes.note: Files with the same size and the same content hash are duplicates. The copies go to the Trash, so you can restore them.

apps.uninstallDesktop: Lustro shows the command that removes this package.
apps.uninstallStore: Lustro shows the command that removes this app.
apps.note: Lustro lists the apps. To remove one, run the command that Lustro shows.
apps.lastUsedNote: Linux does not record when an app was last used.

live.off: Live updates are not available on Linux yet
